Accepted proof:
Source: step 1 (normalization) of the supplied proof, for an arbitrary open domain U. Hⁿ := μHE[n].
1. Let R₀ be an IMRep in U representing X, with carrier M₀, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Let Z := X.zeroRegion; Z is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion) and spt X = U ∖ Z by definition of X.support. Hence spt X is Borel (U and Z are open).
2. (M_Z(X) = 0.) Let ω be admissible for X.massOn Z, i.e. ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n Z: a test form in U with tsupport ω ⊆ Z and |ω(x)| ≤ 1. Since tsupport ω ⊆ Z is disjoint from spt X = U ∖ Z, (VO) gives X(ω) = 0, so ofReal(X ω) = 0. Thus X.massOn Z, the supremum of these values, is 0.
3. (Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0.) By (MR) for X, R₀ and the open set Z: R₀.measure(Z) = X.massOn Z = 0. Since R₀.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M₀).withDensity θ and Z is Borel, R₀.measure(Z) = ∫⁻_{M₀∩Z} θ dHⁿ. As θ ≥ 1 on M₀ (θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M₀), Hⁿ(M₀ ∩ Z) ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀∩Z} θ dHⁿ = 0. Since M₀ ⊆ U, M₀ ∖ spt X = M₀ ∩ Z, so Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0.
4. (Restriction.) (IMC)(b) with U, R₀ and the Borel set E := spt X gives a current A and an IMRep R in U with R.Represents A, R.carrier = M₀ ∩ spt X, R.mult = θ and R.orient = ξ.
5. (R represents X.) By step 3, M₀ ∩ spt X and M₀ are Hⁿ-a.e. equal, so Hⁿ⌞(M₀ ∩ spt X) = Hⁿ⌞M₀ (Measure.restrict_congr_set). Hence for every test form ω, R.action(ω) = ∫_{M₀∩spt X} θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{M₀} θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = R₀.action(ω) = X(ω).
6. R.carrier = M₀ ∩ spt X ⊆ spt X.
7. (Mass.) (MR) for X, R and the open set U gives X.massOn U = R.measure U, and X.mass is X.massOn U by definition (GeometricCurrentOn.mass). Hence R.measure U = X.mass. ∎
proof_key_steps: spt X = U ∖ zeroRegion is Borel; every form admissible for M_{zeroRegion}(X) is killed by (VO), so M_{zeroRegion}(X) = 0.
(MR) on the open zero region and θ ≥ 1 give Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = 0.
(IMC)(b) with E = spt X restricts the representation; equal restricted measures show it still represents X.
(MR) on U gives R.measure U = M(X).

Source: step 4 of the parent proof (with the n = 0 provisions of its step 10). It plays the role of Simon's decomposition of Lemma 1.2 / Remark 1.3 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–75: M = ⋃_j M_j disjoint, M_j ⊆ N_j, H^n(M_0) = 0), with bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces in place of pieces of C¹ submanifolds; families are indexed by ℕ and empty pieces are allowed. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. Rectifiable cover. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n).
2. Regular sets. Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j). G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s = univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
3. Coercivity constant and radius. For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^n: if n ≥ 1 take m(A) := min{|Ah| : |h| = 1} (the unit sphere is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and positive on it; for h ≠ 0 apply this to h/|h|; h = 0 is trivial); if n = 0 take m(A) := 1 (the only vector is h = 0). (Alternatively m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A from Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, valid in every dimension.) Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Partition. For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and the radius r of step 3 (rpos holds). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}; and if G_j ≠ ∅ then A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j.
5. Bi-Lipschitz pieces. Put D_{j,k} := G_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Claim: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}. If D_{j,k} = ∅ this is vacuous. Otherwise G_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) with y ∈ G_j is injective and ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2; by step 4 and (†), |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular F_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and F_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ G_j.
6. Enumeration. Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := F_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0, and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i Borel and F_i injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. Disjoint pieces. Define B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'} =: P_i, which is Borel and contained in M. 8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)). By step 1, x = F_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ G_j. 4. Part (1). By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}(Σ_I (det V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩))^{1/2} by step 3 (the Gram determinant is ≥ 0, being a sum of squares).
5. Part (2). For n = 0 take α the constant 0-covector with value 1: |α|_E = 1 (𝓘 consists of the empty map) and α() = 1. For n ≥ 1 let α(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}; it is multilinear, alternating and continuous, hence an n-covector, and α(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1. Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), stated there without proof; the argument is the one indicated in Remark 2.6 (properties (a), (b) of the norm) together with 2.7–2.8 (lines 243–283). Write E for the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P with the inner product ⟨α, α'⟩_E := Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) (sum over increasing n-tuples I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n), e_I := (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})); its norm is |·|. If n > P then E = 0, every n-form vanishes, so T = 0 and M_W(T) = 0, and Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P (Hausdorff dimension P < n), so μ_R = 0 and the claim holds. Assume n ≤ P.
1. (Algebra.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩. Expanding each τ_i in the standard basis, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I), where A_I is the n×n submatrix of A with columns I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. The covector α_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} satisfies α_τ(e_I) = det(A_I); hence ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = α(τ) for every α, |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ) = 1. (For n = 0 everything is trivial: α(τ) = α(∅) and |α| = |α(∅)|.)
2. (Consequences on M.) Let J : E* → E be the Riesz isomorphism (⟨α, J(η)⟩_E = η(α)) and β := J ∘ ξ, an Hⁿ⌞M-measurable E-valued map. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) with τ orthonormal, so by step 1: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E, β(x) = ±α_τ, |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1.
3. (Integrability.) For every compact K ⊆ U, μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ (sup|ω|)·θ·1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so the integrand is integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R.
4. (Upper bound.) Let ω be admissible: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, and ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 if x ∉ W. Hence T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W), so max(T(ω), 0) ≤ μ_R(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound: reduction to compact sets.) V := U ∩ W is open and μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) since M ⊆ U. V is the increasing union of the compact sets K_i := {x ∈ V : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/i} (K_i := {|x| ≤ i} if V = ℝ^P), so μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i). It therefore suffices to prove M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for every compact K ⊆ V and every η > 0. Fix K and η; if μ_R(K) = 0 there is nothing to prove.
6. (Open neighbourhood.) Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ V. The sets O_s := {x : dist(x, K) < s}, 0 < s ≤ δ, have compact closures contained in V ⊆ U, so μ_R(O_δ) < ∞ and μ_R(O_s) ↓ μ_R(K) as s ↓ 0 (continuity from above; K is closed). Fix s ∈ (0, δ] with μ_R(O ∖ K) < η, where O := O_s.
7. (Lusin.) μ_R⌞K is a finite Borel measure on a compact metric space and β is μ_R-measurable; by Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01/Lusin.lean) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that β|K' is continuous; by inner regularity we may also assume that |β| = 1 and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1 at every point of K' (these hold μ_R-a.e. by step 2).
8. (Continuous extension.) By Tietze's extension theorem (applied to the coordinates of β in a basis of E), β|K' extends to a continuous g_0 : ℝ^P → E. Let r : E → E be the radial retraction r(α) := α if |α| ≤ 1, r(α) := α/|α| otherwise (continuous, |r| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball). By Urysohn's lemma choose a continuous χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K' and tsupport χ ⊆ O compact. Put g := χ·(r ∘ g_0). Then g is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ O is compact, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, and g = β on K'.
9. (Smoothing.) Let φ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, supported in the closed σ-ball) and g_σ := g * φ_σ (componentwise convolution). Then g_σ is C^∞, tsupport g_σ ⊆ {x : dist(x, tsupport g) ≤ σ} ⊆ O for 0 < σ < dist(tsupport g, ℝ^P ∖ O), |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(x − y)| φ_σ(y) dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_σ → g uniformly as σ ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). Viewed as an n-form, g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (compact support in O ⊆ U) and g_σ is admissible for M_W(T) (O ⊆ V ⊆ W, |g_σ| ≤ 1).
10. (Estimate.) By steps 2–3, |T(g_σ) − ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R| ≤ sup|g_σ − g|·μ_R(closure O) → 0 as σ ↓ 0. On K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ = ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1; on O ∖ K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ ≥ −|g| ≥ −1 μ_R-a.e.; off O, g = 0. Hence ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(O ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − η) − (μ_R(O ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K')) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3η. Therefore max(T(g_σ), 0) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for σ small, and M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.
11. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞); together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W). ∎
Remark (reuse; not a proof step). Step 4 proves M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) and steps 5–11 prove μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) for open W. Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.

By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers).
